Where frequency, volume and recovery line up best

4-Day Workout Split: The Best Routines Compared

Short answer: Upper/lower is the best 4-day split for most lifters: every muscle is trained twice a week, sessions are manageable, and recovery is straightforward.

How a 4-day workout split works

Four days is where training gets flexible enough to give every muscle direct work twice a week without every session feeling endless. For many lifters it is the most productive schedule in terms of results per hour in the gym.

Your options are mainly about how to divide the body. Upper/lower is the cleanest answer, a push/pull/legs plus upper hybrid adds variety, and body-part pairs trade frequency for focus.

Best 4-day split structures

Upper / Lower (recommended)

MonUpper
TueLower
WedRest
ThuUpper
FriLower
SatRest
SunRest

Best for: Most intermediates and many beginners. Each muscle is trained twice a week with two rest days.

Trade-off: Upper days cover a lot of muscles, so exercise selection and time management matter.

Push / Pull / Legs + Upper

MonPush
TuePull
WedRest
ThuLegs
FriUpper
SatRest
SunRest

Best for: Lifters who like PPL but only have four days. Upper body gets twice-a-week frequency.

Trade-off: Legs are trained only once a week, so add a lower-body emphasis to the upper day or choose upper/lower instead.

Body-part pairs

MonChest & Triceps
TueBack & Biceps
WedRest
ThuLegs
FriShoulders & Abs
SatRest
SunRest

Best for: People who enjoy dedicated sessions and higher volume per muscle in one visit.

Trade-off: Each muscle is trained about once a week.

Is a 4-day split right for you?

Beginner friendlyGood (upper/lower)
Muscle buildingExcellent
StrengthExcellent — main lifts twice a week
Schedule flexibilityModerate
Recovery demandModerate
Session length55–75 min
Weekly frequency per muscle2× (upper/lower); 1–2× others

Pros

  • Every muscle trained twice a week (upper/lower)
  • Room for both heavy compound lifts and accessory work
  • Two full rest days
  • Fits most work schedules

Cons

  • Less forgiving of missed sessions than 3-day plans
  • Easy to overload upper days with too many exercises
  • Needs a rough weekly plan for volume

Best for

  • Intermediate lifters wanting steady progress
  • Beginners ready to move up from 3 days
  • Anyone prioritising both size and strength
  • People who like a predictable weekly rhythm

Think twice if…

  • People who can only train irregularly
  • Lifters who want to train each muscle only once per week for time reasons

Recovery on four days

The Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri layout gives each half of the body at least two days before it is trained again, and two full rest days for everything. Sleep and food matter more here than on a 3-day plan because you are doing more total work.

If a session is going badly, trim accessory sets rather than skipping the main lifts — the main lifts drive most of the progress.

Example exercises for a 4-day split

Upper day

Press, pull, overhead press, vertical pull, then shoulder and arm accessories.

Barbell Bench PressBarbell RowBarbell Overhead PressLat PulldownDumbbell Lateral RaiseCable Tricep Pushdown

Lower day

Squat pattern, hinge pattern, then leg isolation, calves and core.

4-day workout split FAQ

What is the best 4-day workout split?

Upper/lower is the best default: each muscle twice a week and balanced recovery. PPL + upper and body-part pairs are valid alternatives depending on preference.

Is a 4-day split better than 5 days?

Not necessarily. Four days is often easier to recover from and sustain, and results depend more on consistency and total volume than on the number of days.

Which days should I train?

Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri works well, but any pattern that separates upper and lower sessions and gives you two rest days is fine.
